JSA Penggalian perlu perbaikan dalam hal kejelasan dari identifikasi bahayanya terhadap aktifitas yang telah disebutkan seperti 1. Perpindahan Dumptruk---belum menyebutkan bahaya tertabrak atau terlindas 2. Dumping--belum menyebutkan bahaya tertimbun atau terbentur.JSA yang tersedia masih belum sepenuhnya saling keterkaitan dengan RP3K dan SWC nya, seperti P3K gigitan binatang berbisa sudah tersedia namun di JSA terkait Biological Hazard belum disebutkan., sedangkan di SWC sudah dicentang.Belum adanya penyediaan Portable Eyewash sebagai alat RP3K dari bahaya kelilipan debu pasir atau debu bahan kimia (semen), fasilitas terdekat berjarak 80m dengan jalan memutar, dan sebaiknya disediakan dilokasi pekerjaan tersebut.Petugas HSSE Metrindo atau PA sebaiknya memiliki kompetensi pelatihan P3K sesuai paparan resiko dilokasi kerja, termasuk P3K untuk kemungkinan tersengat dari kejadian kebocoran arus Listrik.

No documented CSE-specific rescue plan or rescue arrangement was established for two workers inside the hood/above the fan blade. EEBA was available for emergency escape but does not replace rescue preparedness for an incapacitated entrant.
OBS-017 CSE PM fin fan cooler 50%.docx

The PA remained outside the hood and maintained oversight; however, the activity was not recognized as CSE and an emergency egress response was not established. In the event of a PGD alarm, the mobile staircase had to be repositioned to the hood access point, creating potential delay in evacuating the two entrants.

The two workers exposed to hazardous energy were not protected by their own individual locks. Their protection was represented by the PA's lock on the LOTO box. The crew understood this arrangement as compliant with the current SIKA and Energy Isolation TKO and applied a stop-work rule whenever the PA left the worksite. An interpretation/interface gap was identified between the V&V individual protection requirement and the current SIKA–ICC/group lock arrangement.

Fall Restraint vs Fall Arrest Selection

Workers used a fall arrest system; however, they were unable to explain how to determine when fall restraint should be selected instead of fall arrest. The system selection appeared to be based on the fall arrest equipment being available rather than a hierarchy-based assessment of preventing access to the fall hazard first.

Fall Arrest vs Fall Restraint Lanyard
Workers were unable to clearly explain the technical difference between fall restraint, which prevents reaching the fall hazard, and fall arrest, which stops a worker after a fall has occurred.
